text: How does pressing a pedal make a car move? Follow the force, from foot to road.
Gas pedal first. No cable: two sensors read how far you press and tell the engine computer.
A small motor opens the throttle. Air rushes in, and fuel is added, about fourteen point seven to one by weight.
Each spark shoves a piston down. The crankshaft turns those pushes into spin.
The gearbox and differential multiply that twist: about fourteen to one in first gear.
Driveshaft and axles carry it to four hand-sized patches of rubber that push the road back. The car goes forward.
Now the brake. The pedal is a four to one lever: a hundred pound push becomes four hundred.
A vacuum booster uses engine suction to roughly double it. Eight hundred pounds.
That drives a one-inch master cylinder piston into the brake fluid. About a thousand P S I.
Pascal's law: that pressure acts everywhere. On caliper pistons six times bigger, it's five thousand pounds of clamp, roughly.
The pads squeeze the rotors, and motion turns into heat.
What should we take apart next?
Congrats! You've discovered how a pedal moves a car.
